correctness.rationale: Let x=τ/2, R=(I+xL)^−1. The step equals I+2xR′. Cofactors give D=det(I+xL)=1+2(a+b)x+3abx² and R12=ax(1+bx)/D, R23=bx(1+ax)/D, R13=abx²/D. Differentiation yields the three stated off-diagonals for all x≥0; the remote pair is positive at x>0. The multiplier is (1+y²)/(1+y)² for y=xλ≥0, in [1/2,1], so all diagonals are at least 1/2; symmetry and mass conservation follow from the Laplacian. For a≥b the strong-edge numerator after dropping the positive prefactor is (1+bx)²−b(a−b)x²; the opposite-edge quadratic is positive. It stays strictly positive for every finite x when a≤2b, and for a>2b its decreasing linear factor crosses exactly at x=1/(sqrt(b(a−b))−b), while the other factor stays positive. This gives precisely the stated zeros at the cutoff, permanent negativity only across the stronger edge afterward, strict signs at positive steps for the balanced regime, and I at τ=0. On one edge of weight c the off-diagonal is 2cx/(1+2cx)²>0. The Cayley representation follows from Cτ=2R−I, and exact arithmetic confirms the comparator values −9/2809 and 18/1621 at (3,1,6).
